claim:
For the Ray–Ghosh system \(\dot x=-x+y+z\), \(\dot y=xy-z\), \(\dot z=-xz+y+b\) with \(b>0\), the cubic used in the source to parameterize equilibria factors as \((x+1)(x^2-x-b)\), but \(x=-1\) is never an equilibrium; thus the actual equilibrium \(x\)-coordinates are \(x_\pm=(1\pm\sqrt{1+4b})/2\) when \(b
eq2\), while at \(b=2\) only \(x_+=2\) is valid. Every compactly supported invariant probability measure \(\mu\) satisfies the exact stationary law \(\int (x-1/2)^2\,d\mu=b+1/4\). Consequently, for any non-equilibrium ergodic invariant measure its mean \(m=\int x\,d\mu\) obeys \(x_-<m<x_+\) and the measure gives positive mass both to \(x\in(x_-,x_+)\) and to \(x
otin[x_-,x_+]\); every nonconstant periodic orbit crosses at least one algebraic level \(x_-\) or \(x_+\). For \(b
eq2\) both levels are equilibrium \(x\)-coordinates; at \(b=2\), \(x_-=-1\) is only an algebraic threshold and not an equilibrium.

correctness.rationale: Direct equilibrium algebra rules out \(x=-1\) before division; exact polynomial differentiation gives \(\dot F=-2(x^2-x-b)\); compact-support invariance yields the moment identity; variance, endpoint rigidity, and sign-crossing consequences follow without numerical assumptions. The \(b=2\) singular edge is handled explicitly: \(x_-=-1\) remains a zero of the balance polynomial but is not called an equilibrium, and the crossing conclusion is stated in terms of the algebraic levels.
